targets.authors: Alves, H., Koch, A., & Unkelbach, C.
targets.title: A cognitive-ecological explanation of intergroup biases.
targets.evidence_quote:
In our replication, we conducted the same three experiments as versions of a single study.
The three claims we tested compared the tribe choices of participants in the positive
unique conditions to the tribe choices of participants in the negative unique conditions
within each of the three versions of the study. Of these three claims, two did not replicate.
Only the version of the study designed to replicate Experiment 1 of Alves et al. produced a
difference between valence conditions. Participants were more likely to choose the first
tribe when the second tribe shared the same positive traits as the first tribe (i.e., the
negative unique condition; 56.50%) than when the second tribe shared the same negative
traits as the first tribe (i.e., the positive unique condition; 43.09%).
